clips.caption: Ad: Kevin Trudeau on the exact moment you've earned the right to say "I am a millionaire" — and why saying it before you believe it just keeps you stuck. Which stage are you on right now?
Ad: Kevin Trudeau on why the very first step toward a big goal isn't "I want" — it's a much smaller word. Would you actually say it out loud?
Ad: Kevin Trudeau on the picture you carry of yourself, and why saying something that doesn't match it creates conflict instead of results. What does your picture say?
Ad: Kevin Trudeau on why saying "I want to be a millionaire" can trigger old beliefs that fight back. Which belief about money did you grow up with?
Ad: Kevin Trudeau on the difference between "I will" (someday) and "I am in the process" (today). What are you doing right now that proves you're in the process?
Ad: Kevin Trudeau on why "I am a millionaire" is where you finish, not where you start. Where are you on the ladder right now?

Ad: Kevin Trudeau tells the story of the moment he was finally given what he was told was a miracle that takes only five seconds.

He was sitting at the edge of his seat, expecting something huge. The lesson was a single sentence: take 100 percent responsibility for everything that happens in your life, without exception and without condition.

Then everyone stood, shook his hand, and the lesson was over.

Kevin explains that it's quick to hear and takes years to live.

What would change if you took that sentence seriously?

#mindset #responsibility #kevintrudeau

Ad: Kevin Trudeau recalls the classic Earl Nightingale recording, The Strangest Secret: you become what you think about most of the time.

Kevin tells how he laughed when he first heard it, because he was always thinking about girls. Everyone in the room laughed too, but they understood the distinction. You become what you think about and feel about most of the time.

Thoughts are things. So his advice is to control your thoughts and feelings, feel good now, and keep working on being a better you.

What do you think about most of the time?

#mindset #thoughts #kevintrudeau

Ad: Kevin Trudeau shares a small story that shows how distance grows between two people.

A man comes home from lunch and tells his wife where he went and what he ate. Every word is true.

What he leaves out is who he had lunch with. He didn't lie, but he wasn't honest either.

Kevin says there is a real difference between telling the truth and being honest. Small omissions can build a quiet barrier between people.

Where have you noticed the gap between the two?

#relationships #communication #kevintrudeau

Ad: Kevin Trudeau gives a straight answer on whether there is only one soulmate.

His reasoning is simple. If you think there is exactly one person on the whole planet meant for you, that's a stretch.

He compares it to asking whether any other planets could support life. Just look at the odds.

Kevin says there are likely many people you could connect with deeply, and that changes how you think about finding someone.

Do you believe in the one, or in many?

#soulmate #relationships #kevintrudeau

Ad: Kevin Trudeau answers what he would do if he had a roommate who was a slob.

His answer: he wouldn't have that roommate, because he wouldn't be in that situation.

The people around him are honest, kind, loving and good communicators. They don't have buttons that get triggered.

Kevin says that's because of what he is attracting into his life. His view is that the people in your world reflect the person you are.

What does your circle reflect back to you?

#mindset #relationships #kevintrudeau

Ad: Kevin Trudeau looks back at a time when nobody carried a credit card.

Back then you had a charge account at the local store, or a charge card from a handful of companies. It was meant for convenience, so you didn't have to carry a lot of cash.

Kevin explains how different that world was from the one we live in now, and why the difference matters.

What do you think changed most between the charge card era and today?

#credit #money #kevintrudeau

Ad: Kevin Trudeau on the key difference between a charge card and a credit card.

With a charge card, the money had to already be in your bank. Sometimes the company even checked with your bank first.

With a credit card, you can spend money you don't have. Kevin explains that a charge card was just a convenience, while a credit card lets you spend beyond what you hold.

It's a simple distinction worth keeping in mind.

When you use a card, do you check the balance in your account first?

#credit #mindset #kevintrudeau

Ad: Kevin Trudeau on a detail about credit scores that many people miss.

Most of us assume that paying by the due date is all that matters. Kevin explains that the card company usually reports your balance to the credit agencies 10 to 15 days before that date.

His advice is to ask your card company when they report, then pay the balance off before that day.

It's a small timing change, and it's the one Kevin calls the magic secret.

Did you know your report date and your due date can be different?

#credit #creditscore #kevintrudeau

Ad: Kevin Trudeau on a phrase we hear all the time: live within your means.

Kevin says it isn't enough. You have to live below your means.

He points to how his father's generation handled money. They kept housing a small share of income, and they didn't finance cars. They paid cash, and until they could, they went without.

It's an old habit, and Kevin says it's still a strong one.

What's one expense you could trim to live below your means?

#money #mindset #kevintrudeau

Ad: Kevin Trudeau on a rule of thumb for spending.

If you can't pay for something with cash, he says you can't afford it, with the possible exception of a house and a car.

Then he looks at housing itself. Kevin says many people pay too large a share of their income for the home, once you add the mortgage, insurance and upkeep.

He's not a financial planner, and he says so. It's common sense he asks you to apply to your own numbers.

What share of your income goes to housing?

#budget #money #kevintrudeau

Ad: Kevin Trudeau paints a picture of what it feels like to be debt free.

Cards at zero, payments current, and some savings set aside for a rainy day.

Kevin says that kind of order brings a feeling of strength and control, and that confidence carries into every other part of your life.

It's less about the numbers and more about the peace of mind they give you.

What would having zero balances change for you?

#debtfree #mindset #kevintrudeau

Ad: Kevin Trudeau explains what he calls a robust credit file.

His picture is two installment loans, such as a mortgage and a car payment, plus three revolving lines of credit. He says more than that can pull the score down, because it means too much available credit.

He also mentions a home equity line and a line against a stock portfolio. These can sit available without being used.

Which part of your own credit file do you understand least?

#credit #creditscore #kevintrudeau

Ad: Kevin Trudeau on the biggest mistake people make in hard times.

He says it is calling it adversity in the first place. Kevin explains it is simply a situation, and nobody else makes you feel a certain way.

He shares the story of Viktor Frankl, who wrote Man's Search for Meaning while in a concentration camp. Frankl said others could control everything around him, but not his thoughts.

The lesson: you choose what you think, and what you think shapes how you feel.

Where in your life could you choose your thoughts on purpose?

#mindset #kevintrudeau

Ad: Kevin Trudeau tells the story of two men on a porch and an old hound dog that keeps moaning but never moves.

When one man asks why the dog won't get up, the other says he's lying on a nail, but it doesn't hurt him enough.

Kevin says people can be the same. They don't like their house, their car or their situation, but the discomfort never gets big enough to force a change.

A change often starts when staying put hurts more than moving.

What is your version of the nail you keep lying on?

#mindset #motivation #kevintrudeau

Ad: Kevin Trudeau grew up in a blue collar town and wanted to learn how successful people think.

His plan was simple. He became a caddy at a country club where the members were wealthy, and he watched them closely.

He noticed they talked, thought and carried themselves differently. But they were normal human beings, just like his dad.

The real difference was how they thought and how they saw themselves. That is when he realized he could do it too.

Who are you spending your time around?

#success #mindset #kevintrudeau

Ad: Kevin Trudeau grew up in a blue collar community where his dad was a welder and his mom stayed home.

Everyone on the street worked a job, hoped to get into the union and dreamed of a government pension.

Kevin learned early that you have to work for yourself and be your own boss.

That lesson sent him to the library to read about people who became very successful.

What did you learn early about work from the people around you?

#entrepreneur #mindset #kevintrudeau

Ad: Kevin Trudeau tells a story about a friend who taught success seminars but kept stumbling in business.

Every time he looked at a deal he said, "I have a concern." Kevin points out that a concern is fear in words.

His advice was to swap it for "I have a question" or "there's something here we can make better."

The same situation, but now you are the one steering the conversation.

What word do you use out of habit without noticing?

#mindset #communication #kevintrudeau

Ad: Kevin Trudeau on the two most powerful words you use: "I am."

Kevin explains that whatever you put after "I am" is taken by your mind as a statement about your whole being. "I am a loser." "I am a shy person."

Say it often enough and you have spoken it into existence as a fact about yourself. It will not change until you change it with your words first.

It is a short habit to notice, and it can start today.

What do you usually say after "I am"?

If success feels this hard, there may be something you can't see.

Kevin uses a picture to explain counter intentions. You walk toward everything you want and wonder why it is so hard. He says it is like carrying 800 pounds on your back, or walking into a hundred mile an hour wind, and you can't see either one.

His point is that the struggle is not always about effort.

What do you think the invisible weight in your own life might be?

#ad #mindset #success #kevintrudeau

Even after you drop a limiting belief, an old habit can keep running the show.

Kevin explains that things you have done over and over build neural pathways in the brain. If you did something one way for 10, 15 or 20 years, he says you will likely do it again tomorrow, simply because it is a habit.

That is why awareness matters as much as belief.

What is one habit you repeat without noticing it?

#ad #habits #success #kevintrudeau

You can dream big without living in a dream world

Kevin shares what a famous chef told him: have a dream, but do not be delusional about it.

Want a private jet? Great, go look at them and let yourself expand. But then come back to reality and ask what the next logical step is. For someone with no job, that step is simple.

Dream big, then act on the one step in front of you.

What is your next logical step today?

#ad #goals #mindset #success

Why one firm decision can change how you show up

Kevin says the answer to many struggles comes down to choice and decision. His phrase to remember: success is a decision away.

He also shares a line from Mary Kay Ash, who founded Mary Kay Cosmetics: one person with a commitment is more powerful than a thousand people with an interest.

In Kevin's view, the moment you say "I'm going to do it, period," everything else starts from there.

What decision have you been putting off?

#ad #success #mindset #goals

If you will laugh about it later, you can laugh about it now.

Kevin explains that we choose whether we are happy or sad, and nobody can make that choice for us unless we allow it. He paints a picture: a car crash, rain, a deserted road, a dead phone and no help in sight.

The situation is bad either way. What changes is how you meet it. If it will be funny later, it can be funny now.

What would change if you chose your mood first?

#ad #happiness #mindset #kevintrudeau

Viktor Frankl kept one freedom when everything else was taken.

Kevin points to Man's Search for Meaning. If we can control our thoughts, we can control our emotions, even when the conditions do not change.

He adds that there is no real good news or bad news. There is just news, and we put the label on it that makes us happy or sad.

What label are you putting on something right now?

#ad #mindset #happiness #kevintrudeau

Your best ideas rarely show up while you are scrolling.

Kevin explains that breakthroughs and aha moments happen in the pause. They come right before sleep, right before waking, or in the shower, when the mind goes quiet.

In that stillness, the subconscious brings up what you need. Constant doing and thinking leaves no room for it.

When do your best ideas usually show up?

#ad #mindset #habits #kevintrudeau

The biggest prayer mistake starts with a feeling, not a word.

Kevin explains that most people pray from desperation, lack and fear. They ask for one specific result because they believe it will finally make them feel better.

That sense of need, he says, is exactly what gets in the way of a calm, clear connection.

When you ask for something, which feeling are you asking from?

#ad #mindset #fear #kevintrudeau

What if your life is bigger than the years you can count?

Kevin explains that most people see life as the time between birth and the end of the body, and treat that as everything.

Asked for one thing worth grasping, his answer is that you create your own reality. He says seeing the bigger picture can leave you feeling less stressed, less confused and less afraid.

It is a short teaching about how you see yourself and your days.

What changes for you when you look at life as a bigger picture?

#ad #mindset #success #kevintrudeau

Why do most people lose money? Kevin names three habits.

He explains the rules he sets before he sits down at a casino table, and they apply to any risk. First, a clear win goal, and he stops the moment he hits it. Second, a loss limit, a stop he never crosses. Third, a time limit, one hour at most.

Kevin calls it a mindset more than a system. Discipline is decided before the game starts.

Which of the three would you find hardest to keep?

#ad #mindset #money #habits

A big dream only works when you come back to earth.

Kevin Trudeau explains the difference between a dream that works and plain delusion. Dreaming big stretches you like a rubber band, but you can't live in the dream world.

After you dream, Kevin says, look at where you are now and ask what the next logical step is. Then set that as your next goal and go after it.

It is a step closer, even if it is not the whole dream yet.

Do you dream big and then take the next step, or only one of the two?

#ad #goals #success #kevintrudeau

Kevin says one book turned a struggling pianist into a star.

Kevin Trudeau tells the story of Liberace. He was flamboyant and had a nice smile, but he was not a very good piano player and was not making it.

Then he read a book called The Magic of Believing. Kevin says that within one year Liberace became one of the best-known entertainers in the world, with his own TV show.

What's one book that changed how you think?

#ad #mindset #success #kevintrudeau

The right goal is big enough to excite you, small enough to hit.

Kevin Trudeau explains the sweet spot for a target: big enough to excite you, but small enough that you know you can actually achieve it.

That is different from the dream. A dream can be huge and far away. The target is the next step that makes you say, I can do that.

Is your current goal in the sweet spot?

#ad #goals #success #kevintrudeau

If you want to be interesting, be interested.

Kevin Trudeau shares a story from a lecture on Dale Carnegie's How to Win Friends and Influence People. Carnegie's point is that we have two ears and one mouth and should use them in proportion.

Ask questions and listen more than you talk, because everyone's favorite subject is themselves. Get people talking about themselves and they will like you.

Who is the best listener you know?

#ad #relationships #love #kevintrudeau

You can stop drifting once you find the key to the motor.

Kevin Trudeau uses a simple picture. You are in a boat with no motor and no sail, and the wind and waves push you wherever they like.

Then you realize you hold the key. You turn the motor on, put the throttle down, and you are at cause over the waves instead of at effect.

Kevin says the same is true of life. Taking control starts with knowing you have the power.

Where in your life do you feel at the mercy of the waves?

#ad #mindset #success #kevintrudeau

Money doesn't give you the attitude. The attitude gives you the money.

Kevin Trudeau says most people think they will feel better once they have the car, the house and the life they want.

He says that is backwards. When he lived in a small one bedroom apartment, he still told himself he loved his life and loved being himself.

A wealthy man once told him to walk into a place like he owns it. Kevin objected that he would have that attitude if he had the money. The man said the attitude comes first.

Can you feel good now, before anything changes?

#ad #money #mindset #kevintrudeau

The best player ever also missed the most winning shots.

Kevin Trudeau points out that Michael Jordan made the game-winning shot more times than anyone in basketball history, and also missed it more times than anyone.

Winners are not people who never miss. They are people who keep taking the shot. You miss every shot you don't take.

Kevin says it isn't win or lose. You either win or you learn.

What shot are you afraid to take right now?

#ad #success #mindset #kevintrudeau

Why being someone's better half may not be love.

Kevin Trudeau says you shouldn't want a partner to be your better half. Each person should be whole, not needing the other.

Together, he says, two whole people create a new entity called us. If you are fine on your own, you don't need a partner clinging to you.

Kevin says a power couple comes from feeling good about who you are, not needing anything to complete you.

Do you see a partner as your other half or as a teammate?

#ad #love #relationships #kevintrudeau

One changed word turned a silent ad into a busy mailbox.

Kevin Trudeau tells a story from his early business days. He ran a classified ad and got zero orders while spending money on it.

Then he says he cleared an inner block, felt it lift, changed one word in the same ad, and orders began arriving every day.

Kevin says he went on to build a mail order business before he turned 18.

What small change could shift your next result?

#ad #business #success #kevintrudeau

You can't change a habit you never even notice.

Kevin Trudeau describes a one-on-one session where a man said something and Kevin stopped him. He asked the man to repeat what he had just said. The man couldn't.

Kevin then repeated the eight words for him. They were a statement that he was going to fail. The man had no idea, because it was pure habit.

Kevin's point: the first step is noticing what you say out of habit.

What do you catch yourself saying without thinking?

#ad #habits #success #mindset

Anyone can love life with a jet and a mansion. What about prison?

Kevin Trudeau asks what kind of life you want. Then he flips the question: it's easy to say I love my life when everything is going well.

But what if you were walking into prison to serve ten years? Kevin says the real difference is being able to say I love my life and I love being me, even then.

Is your happiness tied to your situation?

#ad #happiness #mindset #kevintrudeau

Most people never get precise about what they want.

Kevin Trudeau gives the basic manifesting formula in simple steps. First, know exactly what you want. Then see yourself in possession of it in your mind's eye, and feel it as if it were already yours.

Hold that for about a minute, then release attachment to the outcome. Kevin says you repeat this cycle several times a day.

How clearly can you describe what you want?

#ad #goals #mindset #kevintrudeau

A tiny trailer, an old car, heavy debt. The same joy?

Kevin Trudeau says that once you can truly say I love my life and I love being me, outside conditions stop being the point.

He describes it as a fun game. Whether you are in a small trailer with a beat-up car and credit card debt, or in a big house, you feel the same way.

Kevin says conditions can still change. They just don't run your mood.

Could you feel the same with or without the things you want?

#ad #happiness #freedom #mindset

The need fades when the good feeling comes first.

Kevin Trudeau points to the apostles asking Jesus how to pray, and to Mark 11:24, which he reads as saying what you want out loud and also forgiving. He describes a series of steps to make that connection.

His point is that once the connection is made, you stop needing the thing, because you already feel good.

What do you think you need before you can feel good?

#ad #mindset #happiness

Upside down in a Corvette, in the rain, with no phone. Kevin Trudeau laughed.

In 1984 he and his friend Dan were headed out in Orlando when the car flipped. They got out safely, soaked, with no cars passing and no cell phones.

Dan was upset. Kevin told him that someday they would look back and laugh, so why wait? Whether he was happy or sad, the situation would stay the same, so he chose to enjoy the moment.

When something goes wrong, do you choose your mood or let it choose for you?

#ad #happiness #mindset #kevintrudeau

Look around any airport gate. Almost everyone is staring at a screen.

Kevin Trudeau says we are being programmed to constantly be doing and thinking. He calls the cell phone a great tool and also a great trap, because it keeps so many people hooked on the device.

He describes sitting at the airport, looking around, and not finding a single person who was not on a phone, except him.

When did you last sit for a while with no screen at all?

#ad #habits #mindset #kevintrudeau

Are you a snipe? Zig Ziglar had a name for it.

Kevin Trudeau recalls his friend Zig Ziglar, author of See You at the Top. Zig warned him to beware of becoming a snipe, which stands for susceptible to the negative influence of other people.

Kevin says most people today are more susceptible to it than ever before in his memory. The people around you shape your thinking, whether you notice it or not.

Who influences your thinking the most?

#ad #success #mindset #kevintrudeau

An old belief about money can quietly work against you.

Kevin Trudeau explains that someone in a family line may have absorbed the belief that money is the root of all evil. He says that kind of belief can sit in the background for generations.

In his teaching, it works as a hidden counter intention: you say you want wealth while an old belief says wealth is bad.

What belief about money did you grow up hearing?

#ad #money #mindset #success

Beauty may be one of the simplest ways to lift your energy.

Kevin Trudeau explains that art, nature, flowers or a painting send a high-frequency wave into your field, similar to love.

He adds that you do not need to clear every old block. If only part of the resistance is working against you, life takes less effort.

What beautiful thing lifts your mood?

#ad #mindset #energy #happiness

The more specific your wish, the luckier you get.

Kevin Trudeau says step one of luck is knowing exactly what you desire. Wanting just "happiness" is a start, but the clearer you get, the better.

He uses relationships as the example: get clear on the kind of relationship you want and the kind of person you want to be with.

How clearly can you describe what you really want?

#ad #goals #love #kevintrudeau

The self-image that decides how lucky you feel.

Kevin Trudeau explains that everyone carries a mental self-image in great detail, with emotions and thoughts attached.

He compares it to the film in a projector. Whatever you project passes through that image first, so your world becomes a projection of what is inside.

Kevin says if you see yourself as worthy and entitled to be lucky, that is what comes back.

What picture of yourself do you carry?

#ad #confidence #mindset #kevintrudeau

Everything in the universe vibrates. Even your brain.

Kevin Trudeau says every atom has its own frequency, and frequencies either attract or repel one another. That is why some atoms bind together and others push apart.

He adds that the brain broadcasts frequencies too, and he claims what you broadcast affects the physical world around you.

What frequency do you think you broadcast most days?

#ad #mind #energy #kevintrudeau

Most people don't realise they can choose how they feel.

Kevin Trudeau says you can go through life choosing your thoughts, your words and your actions on purpose, and that lets you choose how you feel.

Imagine deciding to feel happy. Or giving anger one minute, then stopping.

Kevin says most people feel angry, sad or full of loss and never see they're in control. They let their mind control them.

When did you last feel truly in charge of your own mind?

#ad #mindset #happiness

Positive thinkers often skip this important step.

Kevin Trudeau says the spiritual masters did two things when hard times came. First, they acknowledged how they felt instead of denying it. Kevin says most people deny their feelings, especially positive thinkers who try to reframe everything.

Second, they welcomed the challenge instead of resisting it. What you resist will persist.

Are you resisting something in your life right now, or welcoming it?

#ad #mindset #confidence

You don't have to reinvent the wheel. You have to pick the right team.

Kevin Trudeau points to Carnegie, Morgan and Rockefeller. The people who rose beside them did it by saying "I'm with you." They did not try to be the star.

Kevin explains that the same goes for Tom Brady or Michael Jordan. If you want to win, get on the team of someone who already wins.

He says he never had to be the guy. He just had to be on the train.

Who is the winner you would want on your team?

#ad #success #mindset

You can't plant tomato seeds and expect oranges.

Kevin Trudeau says success is planting seeds and cultivating the crop. If you want oranges, you have to plant an orange tree seed. Then you can't expect fruit tomorrow.

You water it, you fertilize it, you trim it as it grows, and you let it become a tree. Kevin explains that there is a time for planting and a time for harvest.

The point is to plant the right seed and give it time.

What seed are you planting right now?

#ad #success #mindset

Why do ads make us spend money we don't have?

Kevin Trudeau says people get hypnotized by advertising and keep using their credit cards even when they can't afford it. He points to buying things we don't need to impress people we don't even like.

His point is that the issue is often spending habits, not only what comes in.

What is one purchase you made just to impress someone?

#ad #debt #money #kevintrudeau

Paying on the due date and paying before the reporting date are not the same.

Kevin Trudeau explains that he keeps a mortgage and a car payment on purpose to support a good credit rating. He also uses a few credit cards, pays them off, and always pays before the reporting date, not the due date.

He is describing his own routine, not a promise for anyone else.

Did you know your card has both dates?

#ad #credit #money #kevintrudeau

Living below your means starts with one simple swap.

Kevin Trudeau quotes Jim Carrey: if you won't reduce your lifestyle for a year or two to build one that lasts, you don't deserve it. Kevin says to practice delayed gratification and live below your means.

His example is a cheaper home and a cheaper car, since insurance, fuel and utilities can drop along with them.

What would you trim first?

#ad #freedom #debt #kevintrudeau

Interest rates used to have a legal ceiling in every state.

Kevin Trudeau explains that decades ago each state capped the interest a lender could charge. Charge more and it was called usury, and you were seen as a loan shark.

He says that when the rate is high enough, paying only the minimum can take 30 years and never pay it off.

Have you ever checked how long minimum payments would take?

#ad #debt #credit #kevintrudeau

The first step to what you want is knowing your pain.

Kevin Trudeau says the first step to creating what you want is knowing your pain. He asks what you are sick and tired of, and what you are completely done tolerating.

He points to places it can hide: money pressure, emotional ups and downs, fitness, or relationships that repeat the same pattern.

Once you know what you will not accept, Kevin says, you can clarify what you do want.

What is the one thing you are finished with?

#ad #success #mindset #kevintrudeau

Ever sense someone walk in without seeing them?

Kevin Trudeau describes a party where your back is to the door. Someone comes in, you feel it, and you turn around to find a celebrity or a wealthy person.

Kevin explains it as essence. He says a big presence is so large that it fills the whole room, and everyone kind of feels it.

It is a vivid way to think about the energy people carry with them.

When did someone's presence last change a room for you?

#ad #success #mindset #kevintrudeau

Why the people around you shape how you think.

Kevin Trudeau shares a saying that your income tends to match the average of your five best friends. He says most people hear it and think they need new friends, because the wrong crowd will drag you down.

He reminds us what our parents said: hang around that crowd and you turn out like them. Kevin says if that is true in the negative, it is true in the positive too.

You can team up with people who have big dreams and want more out of life.

Who are the five people shaping you right now?

#ad #success #mindset #kevintrudeau

What happens when two minds share one clear purpose.

Kevin Trudeau explains the mastermind. Your mind is yours and mine is mine, but when we come together in harmony with the same purpose, we create a separate, connected mind.

He says Henry Ford, J.P. Morgan, Andrew Carnegie and John D. Rockefeller called it the most powerful thing you can have to create wealth. Napoleon Hill wrote about it too.

Who could you build a third mind with?

#ad #wealth #success #kevintrudeau
